historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not resolve the RIO board identity, owner, mux or expected devices and cannot show that any scanned bus is the named segment.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds a useful remote-I/O safety model but may have guessed the acronym; its channel/output assumptions cannot become source truth without the missing specification.
historical_reviews.history: Round-2 retained this exact row UNRESOLVED. No approved RIO definition or board I2C contract was found.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The Wistron I2C rule assigns default BMC/platform ownership but still requires the exact board, controller, bus, address, access path and expected output.

original_test_intent: Preserve an I2C validation requirement for the platform's RIO_BD while explicitly leaving the acronym, physical board function and device coverage unresolved rather than assuming remote or rear I/O.
original_method: Because the source delegates everything to an unavailable specification and does not define RIO, no bus discovery, mux traversal or address transaction is authorized until Engineering identifies the board and supplies the complete contract for fresh review.
manual_activity: Platform owners must define RIO_BD's full name, location/function, hardware revision, I2C owner/topology and expected resources before a safe method can be reviewed.
required_inputs: Authoritative expansion and function of RIO_BD
Independent recovery appropriate to the actual board function
safety_requirements: Do not assume RIO means remote I/O or rear I/O
Do not scan all host-visible buses
Do not infer control/output resources from GPT V2
Do not use force or write-capable transactions
Preserve BMC, board and OS health evidence
Stop on any device, I/O, management or bus change
agent_execution_scope: Reject the global scan and unsupported acronym expansion
engineer_actions: Approve management owner and bus/mux/address map
Define safe register transactions and expected responses

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The loop cannot identify which, if any, host adapter reaches RIO_BD and scans unrelated buses without knowing the board function or reserved endpoints. Truncated address grids cannot prove device identity or satisfy an unstated criterion.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED: define RIO_BD and its specification before selecting any enumeration or probe command.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The literal I2C RIO_BD label and two-minute estimates are preserved; no acronym expansion, device class or target is invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: PENDING RIO BOARD IDENTITY AND I2C CONTRACT
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After Engineering identifies the board, build a board-revision-specific allowlist for its BMC/OOB route and compare only approved identity/status reads with the expected BOM/resource matrix while monitoring the actual function's health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes board identity a prerequisite rather than retrofitting a generic scan or an assumed remote-I/O model.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A responding address cannot prove RIO_BD coverage when the acronym, physical location and device population are unknown.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The blast radius cannot be bounded until the board function is known; it may include platform I/O, indicators, sensors or controls, so generic access is not acceptable.

project_override_considerations: Apply default BMC/platform-management ownership but do not use it to guess RIO_BD identity; require exact controller/bus/address, board specification and expected output.
expected_evidence: Approved RIO_BD definition/specification and fresh review
Complete raw responses mapped to expected devices/resources
Function-specific pre/post state, BMC SEL/SDR and OS health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source is incomplete rather than self-contradictory: RIO_BD and both operative fields depend on an unavailable specification.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target board itself is semantically unresolved, in addition to missing bus and acceptance details. An agent cannot bound blast radius or design a relevant command from the acronym alone.

engineering_decision_request.question: Define Functionality row 1806 Wistron-HW-00008-V003 I2C RIO_BD: authoritative RIO expansion/function/location and board revision, BMC/OOB owner and controller/mux/bus route, address/device/register allowlist, expected responses and function-specific health criteria, stop conditions and independent recovery; preserve Master placeholders and require fresh review.

review_improvement: Detects that GPT V2's remote-I/O interpretation is not source-backed and makes authoritative board identity part of the blocking engineering decision.
independent_technical_reasoning: Acronyms in board designs are project-specific; RIO can plausibly denote different physical functions. That ambiguity changes target devices, expected states and recovery. Since the only procedure and criterion are missing-spec placeholders, accepting the remote-I/O expansion would be an invented scope, while a global scan would not resolve identity.
